title: Wings as Eagles
backstory: Isaiah had already warned King Hezekiah that everything in his house, and even his own sons, would one day be carried away to Babylon (Isaiah 39:6-7). God sends a word of comfort ahead to those weary exiles, who would be saying, My way is hid from the LORD (Isaiah 40:27). They were not forgotten: their God feeds his flock like a shepherd, gathers the lambs with his arm, and carries them in his bosom (Isaiah 40:11).

passages.synopsis: God told his prophet to speak comfort to his people: their hard service was over and their sin was pardoned. A voice cries in the wilderness to prepare the way of the LORD. Grass withers and flowers fade, but the word of our God stands for ever. Like a shepherd, God gathers his lambs in his arms and carries them close.

Isaiah asks who has measured the oceans in the hollow of his hand and weighed the mountains in scales. No one taught God or gave him counsel. Beside him, all the nations together are like a single drop in a bucket. He is greater than everything he has made.

Nothing we could make or imagine compares to God. He sits above the circle of the earth, and its people seem as small as grasshoppers. Lift up your eyes to the stars: he made every one, calls each by name, and not one is missing. Such is the greatness of his power.

God's people felt forgotten, as if their way was hidden from him. But the everlasting God never faints and never grows weary. He gives power to the faint and strength to those who have no might. They that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength and mount up with wings as eagles.

but the word of our God shall stand for ever.

reflection: The grass withers, but God's word stands for ever. Where in your life do you need to wait on the LORD and let him renew your strength?
